analyst_view.overall: Crystal Palace (21st, 5 pts) and Real Sociedad (20th, 5 pts) are level just outside the play-off places, so both need points with two league-phase games left after this one. Palace changed manager last week: Pierre Sage was sacked and Thomas Frank lost his first game 3-2 at Coventry on Saturday, with the club 20th in the Premier League; the numbers know nothing about the change. In Europe Palace are without Adam Wharton (red card) and Yeremy Pino (third yellow), which the numbers do not have on their list, plus Ismaila Sarr, Chadi Riad and Takehiro Tomiyasu; Jean-Philippe Mateta's three-match ban is a Premier League one, so he can play here, and Jorgen Strand Larsen scored on Saturday despite an ankle doubt. Real Sociedad miss Ander Barrenetxea (season), Yangel Herrera and Jon Aramburu, which the numbers count, and also Luka Sucic (illness) and Astiazaran, which they do not. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals (Palace 2.2) and already count Barrenetxea and Herrera out for Real Sociedad and Aramburu missing from their defence. What they do not see is that Palace lose Pino, a regular scorer who set up and scored at Coventry, and Wharton, their main passer from midfield, to UEFA bans, while Sociedad also lack Sucic; Mateta being available in Europe is no change for the numbers, which never took him off. So I go lower, to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already nudged up for Real Sociedad's recent corner count (40 in six games) and for Palace conceding many lately. Losing wide players on both sides (Pino, Sarr, Barrenetxea) could trim crossing a little, but Frank's sides have usually leaned on set pieces and direct wide play, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and already lift both sides for recent card counts; Palace picked up 15 bookings in six games under Sage. Wharton and Pino, two of the players booked or sent off lately, are out, which could calm things slightly, but this is a tense game between two sides level on points and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, with Real Sociedad's very busy recent shooting (106 in six games) already adding about 19% to their side. Palace lose two of their main creators in Pino and Wharton and Sociedad are without Sucic, none of which the numbers know, so I shade it to about 26.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, already lower for Palace's quieter recent attack. With Pino and Sarr out, Strand Larsen carrying an ankle problem and Sucic missing for Sociedad, the quality of chances should drop a little, so I go to about 8.9.
